chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him), regarding the man who divorces the young girl who has not yet reached the age of bearing children, and he had consummated the marriage with her; and the woman who has despaired of menstruation, and her menstruation has ceased, so she cannot bear children. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no waiting period upon them, even if he had consummated the marriage with them both.'
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from one of our companions, similar to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a divorced pre-pubescent girl or menopausal woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the fiqh of 'iddah by distinguishing between the general rule of three menstrual cycles and the specific exception for those who do not menstruate, a principle derived from Surah At-Talaq. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physiological state of the woman—specifically the cessation or absence of menstruation—as the primary determinant for the waiting period, even in cases of consummated marriage with pre-pubescent or menopausal women.
